What each NEEDS-YOU needs:
- B02, surname at birth: I don't know whether your family name has ever changed. If it hasn't, leave the field blank or repeat your current surname, whichever the visa centre prefers. If it has, write your former family name.
- B06, country of birth: not in your details. Write the country you were born in.
- B07, nationality at birth and other nationalities: fill these only if your nationality at birth wasn't Filipino, or if you hold another nationality. Otherwise leave them blank.
- B11, national identity number: not in your details. If you have a Philippine national ID (PhilSys) number, you can write it in by hand. If not, leave the field blank.
- B19, e-mail address: not in your details. Add it after the address.
- B20, Employment Pass number and expiry date: copy them by hand from your Employment Pass card.
- B22, employer: write the name, address and phone number of the hospital or clinic you work for in Singapore.
- B32 and B33, accommodation: write the name, address, e-mail and phone number of your hotel or other place to stay in Italy. If you'll stay in several places, list each one, or write the first one and attach the rest of your bookings.
- B36, means of support: tick how you'll pay, e.g. Cash, Credit card, Pre-paid accommodation or Pre-paid transport. Tick all that apply.
- B39, place and date: write the city where you sign, probably Singapore, and the date, on the day you sign.

Things to check by hand:
- B03, given names: I wrote only your first name. Philippine passports print the middle name (usually your mother's maiden surname) on its own line, separate from the given names. Fields 1 to 3 must match the passport, so copy exactly what is printed under "Given names". If the Italian visa centre asks for your middle name too, add it after your first name.
- B04 and B14, dates: the form wants day-month-year. Your passport may print dates with a month abbreviation, e.g. "14 MAR 1990". Either way, check that each date reads in day-month-year order. If it doesn't, rewrite it that way by hand.
- B12: I ticked "Ordinary passport" because that is the standard Philippine passport. If yours is a diplomatic or official one, tick that box instead.
- B26: if your flight changes planes at another Schengen airport (e.g. Frankfurt, Paris or Amsterdam) before Rome, the first entry is that country, not Italy. Write that country instead.
- B27: single entry suits one 14-day holiday. If you plan more Schengen trips, you can ask for multiple entries, but you'd then need to show travel medical insurance for all of them.

As a Singapore resident, you would usually apply through the Italian visa centre in Singapore. Bring your Employment Pass, your flight and hotel bookings, travel medical insurance and proof of funds.
